title: Interleaved Selective State Space Models for Efficient WiFi-Based 3D Multi-Person Pose Estimation
claim: A dual-stream state-space pipeline turns raw sensor signals into predictions, and it beats a heavier baseline on accuracy with far fewer parameters.
layout: Pipeline in a clockwise loop from top-left, with a results panel at bottom-left
description: The figure has two halves. The top and right show the pipeline. At top left, a boxed 'CSI Input' scene shows two WiFi routers (Ntx, Nrx) with dotted red arrows around three black human silhouettes. An arrow labelled CSI leads to a dashed 'WiFi-Mamba' container. Inside it, a red box holds 3D surface plots for Amplitude |H| (blue/purple) and Phase ∠H (orange/red). An arrow leads to an orange 'Dual-Stream Selective SSM' box with Amplitude and Phase pills joined by a coupling symbol, a Fusion node, and a Joint/Conf decoder. A long arrow labelled 'Hungarian' runs down the right side to a gold-bordered 3D plot of three skeleton figures. At bottom left, a rounded panel of paired bars compares MPJPE in mm for 1, 2 and 3 persons (cyan ours vs red baseline), with a Params bar below (2.14 vs 48.2). The eye goes first to the colorful bars and the surface plots.
caption: WiFi-Mamba for 3D multi-person pose estimation. WiFi routers capture CSI encoding human motion. Our dualstream architecture processes amplitude and phase through selective SSMs with cross-stream coupling, achieving linear complexity O(n). WiFi-Mamba achieves 16-27% MPJPE improvements across scenarios while using only 4.4% of baseline parameters.
abstract: WiFi-based human pose estimation offers privacy-preserving and occlusion-robust sensing, but current Transformer-based approaches suffer from quadratic complexity and lack explicit inductive biases for the structure of Channel State Information (CSI). We propose WiFi-Mamba, the first State Space Model (SSM) architecture for WiFi-based 3D multi-person pose estimation. Our approach introduces three key contributions: (1) a Dual-Stream Selective SSM that processes amplitude and phase through parallel pathways with cross-stream state coupling to respect their distinct physical properties, (2) Selective State Attention for pose query decoding with SSM-derived sequential context, and (3) Persistent SSM Memory for temporal consistency across frames without recurrent memory explosion. Extensive experiments on the Person-in-WiFi 3D dataset, covering both single-person and multi-person, demonstrate a 16-27% MPJPE reduction across varying numbers of persons while using only 4.4\% of the baseline parameters (2.14M vs. 48.2M), achieving superior efficiency-accuracy trade-offs particularly beneficial for edge deployment in privacy-sensitive continuous monitoring scenarios.
